To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the presence of ≥5 metastatic pelvic lymph nodes (PLNs) was associated with a high risk of para-aorta lymph node metastasis (PANM) in early-stage cervical cancer, and that the presence of 3–4 metastatic PLNs may warrant consideration for a more aggressive treatment approach, including a para-aortic lymphadecomy.

quality and quantity metrics of lymph node metastasis were significantly associated with para-aortic lymph nodal metastasis and that the risk of para-aortical lymph node metastasis was significantly higher in the group with a high quality and quantity of lymph node metastases than in the other groups.
the number of positive pelvic lymph nodes and the ratio of positive to negative pelvic lymph nodes are useful metrics in identifying patients with a high risk of PAN metastasis.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current evidence does not support the routine use of para-aortic nodal assessment in women with early-stage disease [3, 4].
there is no evidence that the performance of a systematic para-aortic lymphadectomy in early stage cervical cancer is beneficial.
the role of para-aortic node dissection for early-stage cervical cancers has yet to be defined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there is no evidence to recommend routine use of para-aortic nodal dissection (PAND) for early-stage cervical cancers, but there is a role for selective use of this procedure in patients with a high risk of PAN metastasis.

the risk of para-aortocaval (PAC) lymph node metastasis (LNM) was significantly lower than that of pelvic LNM, and the PAC metastasis rate was significantly higher in women with ≥5 pelvic LNM compared with those with <5 pelvic LNM.
we found that the risk of metastasis to the para-aortic nodes (PANMs) was low, and the benefit of para-aortic node dissection in terms of improving survival is unclear [3].
The main takeaway from our work is that
the number of positive pelvic lymph nodes (PLNs) is a useful predictor of the risk of para-aorta lymph node (PAN) metastasis in women with stage IB–IIC cervical cancer.
the number of pelvic lymph node (PLN) metastases is the most significant factor for predicting the presence of PAN metastasis.
we have developed a model that predicts the risk of PAN metastasis and we hope that it can be used as a decision-making tool in the clinic.
